{{ElectionsWI}}
The '''2026 Wisconsin gubernatorial election''' is scheduled to take place on November 3, 2026, to elect the [[governor of Wisconsin]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] Milwaukee County executive [[David Crowley (Wisconsin politician)|David Crowley]] and [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] U.S. representative [[Tom Tiffany]] are the nominees for their respective parties. Incumbent Democratic governor [[Tony Evers]] declined to seek re-election to a third term.

[[Primary elections]] were held on August 11, 2026. Tiffany won the Republican nomination without serious challenge.<ref name=KremerWPR /> Crowley, despite having temporarily withdrawn his candidacy, won the Democratic nomination in an [[upset victory]] over state representative [[Francesca Hong]], receiving 39.8% of the vote.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mueller |first=Julia |title=Crowley defeats democratic socialist Hong to face Tiffany in Wisconsin governor's race |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6023019-crowley-wins-wisconsin-governor-primary/ |access-date=August 12, 2026 |website=The Hill |date=August 12, 2026 |language=en-US}}</ref>

This is the first Wisconsin gubernatorial election since [[2010 Wisconsin gubernatorial election|2010]] in which the incumbent is not seeking re-election,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Beck |first=Molly |title=Wisconsin's Democratic Gov. Tony Evers won't seek a third term in 2026 |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/news/politics/2025/07/24/wisconsin-democratic-gov-tony-evers-wont-seek-re-election-in-2026/84246291007/ |access-date=February 4, 2026 |website=Journal Sentinel |language=en-US}}</ref> along with being one of five Democratic-held governorships up for election in 2026 in a state won by [[Donald Trump]] in the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 presidential election]].<ref name="Gilbert 2024">{{Cite web |last=Gilbert |first=Craig |title=Gilbert: How small voting shifts made Wisconsin the closest state in the nation |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/news/politics/elections/2024/11/25/gilbert-small-voting-shifts-made-wisconsin-2024s-closest-state/76461074007/ |website=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]] |language=en-US |date=November 25, 2024 |access-date=November 26, 2024}}</ref>

If elected, Crowley would be the first African-American governor of Wisconsin. 
{{toclimit|4}}

== Background ==
Wisconsin is considered to be a [[purple state]] at the federal and state levels with a uniquely competitive track record (presidential races decided by less than a point in [[2016 United States presidential election in Wisconsin|2016]], [[2020 United States presidential election in Wisconsin|2020]], and [[2024 United States presidential election in Wisconsin|2024]]; Senate races decided by roughly a point in [[2022 United States Senate election in Wisconsin|2022]] and [[2024 United States Senate election in Wisconsin|2024]]; and a governor's race decided by a point in [[2018 Wisconsin gubernatorial election|2018]]).<ref name="Gilbert 2024" /> The past two federal election cycles in Wisconsin featured split outcomes, with Democrats winning for governor and Republicans for Senate in [[2022 Wisconsin elections|2022]] and Democrats winning for Senate and Republicans for president in [[2024 Wisconsin elections|2024]]. Wisconsin has voted with the winner of the last five presidential elections, and in 2024 it had the second-highest voter turnout in the country (behind [[Minnesota]]) and one of the biggest turnout increases in the country.<ref name="Gilbert 2024" /> Both parties have seen success in the state in recent years. Republicans narrowly control both chambers of the [[Wisconsin Legislature]] and hold a majority in Wisconsin's [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House]] delegation. However, Democrats control most statewide executive offices and have won the last two gubernatorial races.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Unger |first=Nancy C. |title=How Wisconsin Became the Ultimate Purple State |url=https://time.com/7093734/wisconsin-purple-state-history/ |website=[[TIME Magazine]] |language=en |date=October 28, 2024 |access-date=May 28, 2025}}</ref>

Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] governor [[Tony Evers]] was first elected in [[2018 Wisconsin gubernatorial election|2018]], narrowly defeating incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Scott Walker (politician)|Scott Walker]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gowen |first=Annie |title=How the Democrats finally defeated Wisconsin Gov. Scott Walker |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/how-the-democrats-finally-defeated-wisconsin-gov-scott-walker/2018/11/07/3377ed17-9cbe-4537-8b2a-acd0c37a8d35_story.html |url-access=registration |date=November 7, 2018 |access-date=May 28, 2025 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}}</ref> He was re-elected by a slightly larger margin in [[2022 Wisconsin gubernatorial election|2022]], defeating Republican businessman Tim Michels.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bosman |first=Julie |date=November 9, 2022 |title=Tony Evers and Ron Johnson Keep Their Seats in Wisconsin |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/11/09/us/politics/wisconsin-tony-evers-ron-johnson.html |access-date=May 28, 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> In July 2025, Evers announced he would not seek re-election to a third term. The race is widely seen as a tossup due to Evers's retirement and the state's even partisan lean.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cavalli |first=Samantha |date=July 25, 2025 |title=Political analysts call governor's seat 'a toss-up' after Evers decides to not run for a 3rd term |url=https://www.wbay.com/2025/07/25/political-analysts-call-governors-seat-toss-up-after-evers-decides-not-run-3rd-term/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250730005208/https://www.wbay.com/2025/07/25/political-analysts-call-governors-seat-toss-up-after-evers-decides-not-run-3rd-term/ |archive-date=July 30, 2025 |access-date=March 5, 2026 |website=WBAY.com}}</ref>

==Democratic primary==
=== Governor ===
Tony Evers's decision not to seek re-election triggered a competitive Democratic primary.<ref name=BauerAP /> The Associated Press described the process leading up to the August 11 primary as chaotic.<ref name=BauerAP>{{cite web | title=Wisconsin's 2026 primary election arrives with high-profile races for governor, two congressional seats | url=https://pbswisconsin.org/news-item/wisconsins-2026-primary-election-arrives-with-high-profile-races-for-governor-two-congressional-seats/ }}</ref> Lieutenant Governor Sara Rodriguez amassed support as a centrist candidate until she dropped out in mid-July, prompting Milwaukee County executive David Crowley to re-enter the race ten days after withdrawing.<ref name=BauerAP /> The race became a showdown between Crowley, who was endorsed by Evers and other establishment figures, and state representative Francesca Hong, a [[democratic socialist]].<ref name=BauerAP /> Crowley narrowly won the Democratic nomination in an [[upset victory]] over Hong, as polls showed him trailing Hong by nearly 20 points just a week earlier.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Wagner |first1=Bayliss |last2=Igielnik |first2=Ruth |date=2026-08-12 |title=Why Were Polls So Wrong in the Wisconsin Governor's Race? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/12/us/politics/crowley-hong-wisconsin-governor-primary-polls.html |access-date=2026-08-12 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

== Republican primary ==

Tom Tiffany, a member of the [[House Freedom Caucus]], was expected to obtain the nomination without meaningful challenge.<ref>{{cite web | title=Wisconsin's Democratic showdown between Francesca Hong and David Crowley and more races to watch today - CBS News | website=[[CBS News]] | date=August 11, 2026 | url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/wisconsin-governor-democratic-primary-francesca-hong-david-crowley-minnesota-graham/ }}</ref> Tiffany received an endorsement from Donald Trump, who Tiffany believes may have won the 2020 presidential election.<ref name=KremerWPR>{{cite web | title=As the Democratic primary heats up, Republican Tom Tiffany has campaigned for governor on his own terms | date=July 20, 2026 | url=https://www.wpr.org/news/republican-tom-tiffany-campaign-wisconsin-governor-primary-2026 }}</ref> As a member of the federal House, Tiffany objected to the certification of Pennsylvania's and Arizona's electoral results on January 6, 2021, and was prevented from objecting to Wisconsin's electoral results because the [[January 6 attack|Capitol building was stormed by pro-Trump insurgents]].<ref name=KremerWPR /> He has kept mention of Trump to a minimum during his primary campaign.<ref name=KremerWPR />
